source_text:
Hymnus
ΓΕΩΡΓΙΟΙΟ ΑΛΙΤΡΟΙΟ ΥΜΝΟΣ
Μνώεο, Χριστέ, υἱὲ θεοῖο ὑψιμέδοντος, οἰκέτεω σέο κῆρ' ἀλιτροῖο γράψαντος
τάδε· καί μοι ὄπασσον λῦσιν παθέων κηριτρεφέων, τά μοι ἐμφύει ψυχᾷ ῥυπαρᾷ· δὸς
δὲ ἰδέσθαι, σῶτερ Ἰησοῦ, ζαθέαν αἴγλαν σάν· ἔνθα φανεὶς μέλψω ἀοιδὰν ψυχᾶν
παίονι, παίονι γυίων πατρὶ σὺν μεγάλῳ πνεύματι θ' ἁγνῷ.
thought_title: Petition for cleansing, vision, and praise
orientation: Georgius Peccator, the poet, is praying to Christ in the closing section of his hymn, asking for release from passions, vision of divine light, and the ability to sing praise to the Father and the Holy Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: Hymn. Hymn of Georgius the sinner. Remember, Christ, Son of God the most high, your servant's heart, a sinner's, having written these things; and grant me release from heart-bred passions, which grow in my impure soul; and grant me to see, Savior Jesus, your holy radiance; there appearing I may sing a song healing for souls, healing for limbs, to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.

choices.why: The glossary decided form is 'most high' for this epithet of God the Father, matching the brief's cast entry for the Father as 'great' and the established rendering in the previous section.
The glossary English for this term is 'sinner', the poet's self-description, and it appears twice in this section (once in the title, once in the body).
The glossary English for this phrase is 'heart-bred passions', matching the brief's description of inner afflictions bred in the heart.
The glossary English for this phrase is 'impure soul', the defiled soul needing cleansing.
The glossary English for this phrase is 'holy radiance', the divine light of Christ.
The glossary English for this term is 'healing', describing the song as curative for souls and limbs.

pass_b_english: Christ, Son of the most high God, remember your servant's heart—a sinner's heart—that has written these lines. Grant me release from the heart-bred passions growing in my impure soul. And grant me, Savior Jesus, to see your holy radiance, so that, appearing in that light, I may sing a healing song for souls and limbs to the great Father and the pure Holy Spirit.

problems.why: Intro uses different epithet than all hymn sections.

problems.quote: the heart of your servant, a sinner
problems.why: Different phrasing of same self-description across versions.
problems.fix: Flag as manuscript variants, not different content.

variants.text: the heart of your servant, a sinner

problems.quote: Remember, Christ, Son of the most high God, the heart of your servant
problems.why: The opening line is restructured across sections; a reader comparing them may think the meaning shifted.
problems.fix: Use one consistent rendering across all sections or label them as deliberate variants.
